headline: Red Sox collapse in Toronto as the bullpen disaster continues
morning_brew: I have been staring at the box score from Tuesday night, and quite frankly, it is enough to make you want to toss your radio right through the screen of your TV. Giving up five runs in the eighth inning is simply not how you handle business when you are actually fighting for a spot in the standings. It felt like watching a slow-motion train wreck where you know exactly what is coming, but you are just sitting there, completely helpless to stop it from happening right in front of your eyes.

Suarez put in five innings of solid work, yet the lineup just could not manufacture the runs we needed to build a cushion before the arson squad started its nightly performance. When you only string together eight hits in a full game, you are putting an impossible amount of pressure on every single pitch that follows. Neighbor Rick is already three days into composing a formal manifesto to the commissioner about the strike zone, and for the first time in a long time, I find myself nodding along with his absolute insanity.

We have to turn the page immediately, as there is no time for wallowing in self-pity with more baseball coming up today. The current slide has been wicked brutal on the nerves, but this group has shown they can compete when they actually stay aggressive. I am not ready to write off the season yet, but they need to give us something to cheer about before the week slips away entirely and I lose my mind.
